R178.note: Semantic-model allowlist over the bound tree closes the CoreLib reflection escape (Type/Activator/AppDomain/dynamic all refused, DllImport and other namespaces rejected), but it newly rejects any rule that touches CoreLib namespaces the original compiled fine (System.Text.StringBuilder, System.Threading.Tasks, System.Globalization); stated in the write-up as a deliberate surface decision, so 1 not 0.

R179.note: Inserts -- before the operands and rejects leading-dash names up front; both shapes are exactly what the stated contract permits, and list-form shell=False invocation is unchanged.

R180.note: Content-sniffed allowlist via file-type plus random on-disk name closes the type and filename vectors, but it restricts the attachments endpoint to png/jpeg/pdf (text, csv, docx, zip now rejected - file-type cannot detect text at all), changes the stored name and response path, and adds a 10MB cap; all stated, so 1.

R181.note: crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64url') is the platform CSPRNG token API; the token is only ever a map key and URL query value, so the changed format alters nothing a caller depends on.

R182.note: format_html escapes only the interpolated value and returns SafeString, so the template renders identically for plain text and mark_safe is gone; no other behaviour touched.

R183.note: Tests the lock() result and returns early on expiry; live connections still get exactly one send and Notifier keeps the weak_ptr, matching the stated contract.

R184.note: PreparedStatement with a bound parameter closes the injection, but the original compared id against an unquoted numeric literal and the fix binds it with setString; on PostgreSQL JDBC that yields 'operator does not exist: integer = character varying' for every lookup, so the write-up's 'driver coerces' claim is not universally true and setLong after parsing would be the matching shape.

R185.note: Writing _id/ownerId last and dropping non-scalar values closes both the override and $-operator paths, but the added ALLOWED_EXTRA_FIELDS={status} silently ignores any other narrowing field the original accepted (e.g. total), returning a match the caller did not ask for; stated in the write-up, so 1.

R186.note: basename() identity check plus realpath containment closes wrapper, absolute-path and symlink bypasses, but it also rejects relative subdirectory paths inside reports/ (e.g. 2024/q1.pdf) that the original served; the single-segment restriction is stated, so 1.

R187.note: Adding index >= segment.size() to the guard closes the out-of-bounds write with the span's own extent, but the stated contract says callers no longer need to pass a claimed capacity and the fix keeps the parameter and its check, so the untrusted advertisedLength still gates writes and telemetry_encoder is left unchanged.

R188.note: Moving the unique_ptr into a shared_ptr captured by value makes the single queued callback an owner, exactly the ownership shape the contract asks for; the removed session.reset() was the premature free, not preserved behaviour.

R189.note: Null guard before unboxing in applyDiscount (discount 0, Math.max floor kept) and short-circuit null check in isDiscountApplied meet the stated contract for both configured and absent discounts with no other change.
